metadata.document: REPLACING THE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ACT: Risks and solutions

cleaned_body_text: The Environmental Defence Society is conducting a project looking at what the core of New Zealand’s future resource management system should look like. Currently, at the heart of this system is the Resource Management Act 1991, which is the country’s primary environmental and planning law. The RMA is responsible for controlling how land is used, as well as managing more direct impacts of activities on the environment. The RMA has had some successes, but also many problems. The current National-led coalition government intends to replace the RMA entirely with two new statutes based on the enjoyment of property rights: a Planning Act and a Natural Environment Act. The purpose of the EDS project and this report is to explore fundamental issues brought to the surface by phase 3 proposals, supporting government policy development and public engagement.
